deities: Lord Rama (with Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman in the sanctum)

history.dynasty: None (modern; funded by the Thakur Das Sureka family of Howrah)
history.summary: A modern white-marble temple built in 1964 by the Sureka family of Bandhaghat, Howrah (Thakur Das Sureka), inaugurated by President Dr. S. Radhakrishnan. It stands at the spot traditionally held to be where Goswami Tulsidas composed the Ramcharitmanas in the 16th century — the Awadhi retelling of the Ramayana that brought the epic within reach of ordinary people. Its most distinctive feature is its walls: the entire text of the Ramcharitmanas is engraved in marble on two levels of the inner walls, with painted scenes from the epic alongside. The temple also houses a life-size mechanical image of Tulsidas reciting the epic, a library of Ramayana-related literature, a museum of manuscripts and artefacts, and electrified dioramas of mythological scenes (a small fee).

name: Tulsi Manas Temple
town_description: Varanasi (Banaras/Kashi) is one of the world's oldest living cities, on the banks of the Ganga in eastern Uttar Pradesh. The temple stands in the Durgakund area of the southern city, about 250 m south of Durga Kund, ~700 m from Sankat Mochan Temple and ~1.3 km from Banaras Hindu University — usually visited with the Durga and Sankat Mochan temples as one circuit.

travel.airport: Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport, Varanasi (approx. 26-30 km).
travel.railway: Varanasi Junction (approx. 6-7 km); Banaras and Varanasi City stations are alternatives.
travel.road: On Sankat Mochan Road, Durgakund; autos and taxis reach the gate easily. About 1.3 km north of the BHU main gate and 1.5 km from Assi Ghat.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March. Ram Navami (March-April) is the temple's biggest day; the Shravan fair (July-August) features illuminated motorised dioramas.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:30 AM-12:00 PM and 3:30-9:00 PM daily (some sources list the evening session from 3:00 PM — verify). Entry free. Photography allowed in outer areas, restricted inside the main sanctum; bags and cameras not allowed inside.
